rootCauseInvestigation.method: Read the locally stored reply for job aid-417d6dbde712c8747c9f5a17 (conversation b8f5615d-b132-4d90-b85e-ac522b0af808, turn fa06ca3d-1b64-4055-9f99-c6db920959eb) directly from the native per-process conversation snapshot file on Studio 38730's data dir (read-only, local, never committed).
rootCauseInvestigation.finding: The 180-char reply was a COMPLETE, well-formed, SAFE JSON object matching the exact required contract (schema/appId/baseVersion/operations: one add-screen of kind tasks labeled Study Sessions, baseVersion 1) -- not truncated. Every structural double-quote character had been rendered as a Unicode typographic/'smart' quote (U+201C/U+201D) instead of straight ASCII ", which made JSON.parse reject it deterministically. Verified mechanically: raw text failed JSON.parse with a position-1 syntax error; replacing the smart quotes with straight ones parsed cleanly into the exact expected shape.
rootCauseInvestigation.classification: (c) prompt-caused, with (b) as the missing defensive tolerance. Not (a): chars/shape prove the full object was captured, nothing was cut short.
rootCauseInvestigation.whyThePromptCausedIt: buildAiDesignPrompt (src/studio/personal-app-ai-design.mjs, then line 84) told Claude to reply with 'no markdown', so Claude answered in a prose/typeset paragraph rather than literal code. Prose rendering (model styling and/or the provider page's own markdown typography) applies typographic quote substitution that plain JSON text never survives.
rootCauseInvestigation.whyExtractionCouldNotRecover: extractProposalText (src/studio/personal-app-provider-reply.mjs, then line 66) scanned for balanced top-level JSON objects and handed the candidate straight to JSON.parse with no normalization step, so a structurally-complete but typographically-corrupted object was indistinguishable from genuinely invalid JSON.

fix.scope: Smallest existing-file change; no new files.

files.change: Replaced the 'no markdown' instruction with an explicit instruction to put the whole reply inside one fenced code block (described in words -- 'three backtick characters then the word json' -- never typing a literal backtick in the outgoing prompt itself, preserving the existing one-plain-line/no-rich-formatting constraint on OUR typed prompt noted in the adjacent comment) plus an explicit 'use only plain straight double-quote characters, never curly or typographic quotes' instruction. The existing complete minimal example object (schema/appId/baseVersion/one add-screen operation) and the four safe kinds (notes/tasks/dashboard/blank) were already present and are unchanged.

Added straightenQuotes(): a small, lossless normalization (U+2018/U+2019/U+201A/U+201B -> ASCII apostrophe; U+201C/U+201D/U+201E/U+201F -> ASCII double-quote) applied unconditionally to the whole reply text before any fence detection, brace-scanning or JSON.parse attempt. This is defense-in-depth independent of the prompt fix: any future reply (fenced or not, from any provider) that comes back with typographic quotes now still parses. Ambiguity rejection (more than one candidate object/fence) is unchanged; CAS/version/replyDigest/explicit-approval flow is unchanged.
